key_insight: A neural-reparameterized topology optimization method (KATO) can design ship structures that better suppress forced-vibration input power while preserving connectivity and manufacturable feature sizes.
engineering_relevance: This offers a faster way to optimize ship decks and thruster foundations for lower vibration, noise, fatigue, and equipment damage under realistic propulsion loads.
method: Uses a convolutional Kolmogorov-Arnold network (KATO) to parameterize topology.
Optimizes active input power (AIP) under forced vibration, with Helmholtz filtering and Heaviside projection for minimum length scale and manufacturability.
Benchmarked against GCMMA on deck panels and thruster foundation frames, including stress-aware and near-resonant cases.
evidence_signal: Across the tested ship-structure cases, KATO matched GCMMA in AIP within 0.5 dB, reduced binary static compliance by 22-59x in several comparisons, and ran 6.4-10.4x faster in the implemented stress-aware formulations.
watch_item: Performance is reported for specific benchmark geometries and formulations, so transferability to other ship structures, load cases, and fabrication constraints still needs validation.
paper_title: Neural topology optimization of ship structures under propulsion machinery vibrations
